summary: A brownstone tower of 1838 at the mouth of the Connecticut River, replacing a wooden light of 1803; its fifth-order Fresnel lens still shines and Fenwick is set to take it over.

access.note: Reached by a private way; grounds, dwelling and tower closed. Distant views from Neponset Avenue and from river cruises.

notes_for_editor: Thin on primary reports: the local corpus holds almost no Light-House Board text for this station, so the 1855 inspector and 1838 Bache passages are quoted as Lighthouse Friends gives them. Disagreements recorded in the story: first lit 1803/1802; present tower 1838/1839; fourth-order lens date; Whittlesey death 1841/1842; Buckridge arrival 1881/1883; automation 1975/1978; NRHP listing 1989/1990 (the nomination's own record says 29 May 1990, number is 89001469); duplex 1966/1970. Gildersleeve 1915 ice rescue is Lighthouse Friends only. 1924 Bulletin date taken from the volume year. Fifth-order lens 'built 1881' (NRHP) vs installed 1890. USLHS also lists Bill Abrams 1950-1952 whom Lighthouse Friends omits; USLHS 'Henry Clarke' is 'Henry Clark' at Lighthouse Friends. Roster dates were not checked against a primary register. No range or focal height included. Newspaper search (Chronicling America) found only a 1910 navigation notice.
